descript.abstract: This data release provides digital flight line data for a high-resolution airborne magnetic survey over much of the Upper Peninsula of Michigan and nearby parts of northern Wisconsin. The airborne survey was funded by the Earth Mapping Resources Initiative (Earth MRI). The survey was designed by the USGS in collaboration with the Michigan Geological Survey and contracted by the USGS. The survey was designed to meet complementary needs related to geologic mapping and characterization of mineral resource potential. A total of ca. 216,000 line kilometers (km) of magnetic data were acquired over an area totaling ca. 38,400 km^2 across two survey blocks. Data were collected from airplanes flown at a nominal terrain clearance of 100 meters (m) above topography along flight lines spaced at 150 m intervals for Block A (western block) and 400 m intervals for Block B (eastern block). The flight lines were flown N-S. Tie lines were flown E-W every 1500 m for Block A (western block) and every 4000 m for Block B (eastern block). Data were collected by Woolpert, Inc. and EON Geosciences Inc. under contract to the USGS using airplanes with magnetometers mounted in stingers. The survey operated out of airports in Eagle River and Land O’ Lakes, Wisconsin; and Marquette, Escanaba, Kincheloe, Houghton, and Manistique, Michigan, from June of 2025 to October of 2025. Files that are available in this publication include flight line data for the magnetic survey, and reports describing the survey parameters, field operations, quality control and data reduction procedures. A zip file is provided that contains the contractor's deliverable products that includes Geosoft databases and grids for the magnetic survey and reports describing the survey and data reduction. Binary files in this package are readable using the free software "Geosoft Viewer"" or commercial software "Oasis montaj". One or more files contain data available in comma separated value (.csv) file format, GeoTiff raster format (.tif), and geospatial vector format (.shp). The user must have software capable of opening these files.
descript.purpose: The Upper Peninsula region survey was designed to meet complementary needs related to geologic mapping and mineral resource research.
descript.supplinf:
Files that are available in this publication include flight line data for the magnetic survey in an ascii .csv file; flight line data for the radiometric survey in an ascii .csv file; geoTIFF images of the total-field aeromagnetic anomaly, reduced-to-pole (RTP) total-field aeromagnetic anomaly, first-vertical derivative (FVD) of the total-field aeromagnetic anomaly, and potassium, thorium, uranium, and a ternary image; grids of these data; and a report describing the survey parameters, field operations, quality control and data reduction procedures. A zip file containing the contractor's deliverable products is also included. These files are provided as received from the contractor. Binary files in this package are readable using the free software "Geosoft Viewer"" or commercial software "Oasis montaj". One or more files contain data available in comma separated value (.csv) file format, GeoTiff raster format (.tif), and geospatial vector format (.shp). The user must have software capable of opening these files.

overview.eaover: TotalMagAnom_AirborneMagRadUP.png is a Portable Network Graphics (PNG) thumbnail image of the total field magnetic anomaly map in nanoTesla.

BlockA_TotMagAnom_AirborneMagRadUp.tif is a Total Field Magnetic Anomaly (TFA) grid in GeoTIFF format of Block A in WGS84 UTM Zone 16N. Units are in nanoTeslas (nT). GeoTIFF is a public domain metadata standard which allows georeferencing information to be embedded within a TIFF file. GeoTIFF were made using the Minimum Curvature gridding method to create grids of cell size of 37.5 meters (traverse lines only). Point values in this geotiff represent grid values of the data

BlockB_TotMagAnom_AirborneMagRadUp.tif is a Total Field Magnetic Anomaly (TFA) grid in GeoTIFF format of Block B in WGS84 UTM Zone 16N. Units are in nanoTeslas (nT). GeoTIFF is a public domain metadata standard which allows georeferencing information to be embedded within a TIFF file. GeoTIFF were made using the Minimum Curvature gridding method to create grids of cell size of 37.5 meters (traverse lines only). Point values in this geotiff represent grid values of the data.

BlockA_RTP_AirborneMagRadUP.tif is a Reduced to Pole (RTP) grid of the Total Field Anomaly (TFA) of Block A in GeoTIFF format in WGS84 UTM Zone 16N. Units are in nanoTeslas (nT). Reduction-to-pole essentially transforms the data to correct for shifts in anomalies at high latitude, placing the anomaly directly above the source producing body (e.g., Blakely, 1995). An inclination and declination of 72 degrees and -4 degrees, respectively, were used for the transformation. GeoTIFF were made using the Minimum Curvature gridding method to create grids of cell size of 37.5 meters (traverse lines only). Point values in this geotiff represent grid values of the data.

Reduction-to-pole essentially transforms the data to correct for shifts in anomalies at high latitude, placing the anomaly directly above the source producing body (e.g., Blakely, 1995). GeoTIFF were made using the Minimum Curvature gridding method to create grids of cell size of 37.5 meters (traverse lines only). Point values in this geotiff represent grid values of the data.

BlockA_FVD_AirborneMagRadUp.tif is the first vertical derivative of the reduced-to-pole magnetic anomaly for Block A in WGS84 UTM Zone 16N. The first vertical derivative emphasizes short-wavelength features in the data, which is useful in geologic interpretation (e.g., Blakely, 1995). GeoTIFF were made using the Minimum Curvature gridding method to create grids of cell size of 37.5 meters (traverse lines only). Point values in this geotiff represent grid values of the data.
